findings.claim: A dall-e url-mode response hands user code an image whose base64() is "" silently: `_oai_images_block` wraps the URL via `Image.from_url(location, mime)` and the runner delivers it as the `-> image` value with empty bytes and a URL that OpenAI documents as expiring in 60 minutes.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe P1 (scratch project, mock returning {"data":[{"url":"https://oaidalle.example.net/img-1.png"}]}, client response_format="url"): result was `b64=[]|url=[https://oaidalle.example.net/img-1.png]|mime=[image/png]` — no error, empty bytes. openai-openapi Image schema: "the URL of the generated image ... URLs are only valid for 60 minutes". Only reachable when the user explicitly sets response_format="url" (or via request_body), since _oai_images_response_format defaults dall-e to b64_json (ns_internal/images.baml:190-198) — but the client accepts "url" without warning and then silently degrades.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_oai_images_block`, fetch-and-inline url datums (ai.wire.resolve_media with fetch_url=true already implements exactly this), or throw ai.errors.InvalidRequest at render time when response_format="url" is configured for a media-shaped output.

findings.claim: The runner's mixed shape (`-> string | image`) produces a value user code cannot consume through the type system: for a union value holding an image, `v is image` and `v is string` are BOTH false, and a match silently falls through to the string arm, stringifying the image as "Image { _data: <rust_data> }" — silent data corruption in ordinary user code.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe P9: `match (v) { let i: image => ..., let s: string => ... }` on a turn holding one image printed `string-arm text=[Image { _data: <rust_data> }]|is_image=false|is_string=false`. This is the compiler-level primitive-media-union narrowing bug already filed in EXECUTION-STATUS.md:59 item (1); it is NOT in PLAN §6. The workaround documented at crates/baml_tests/baml_src/ns_llm_images/images.baml:260-269 (read the value through baml.json.to_json envelope) HOLDS — probes P2/P13 show correct {kind,source,value,mime} envelopes for both `image | string` (reversed order also recognized) and `(string | image)[]`. Runner-side construction is correct; the shape is unusable idiomatically until the compiler bug is fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the VM/compiler union narrowing for primitive media unions (tracked bug), or until then have _media_shape refuse mixed:image with a clear error pointing at the envelope workaround, so users don't silently ship the string-arm fall-through.

findings.claim: The gateway client drops the response's `usage` object entirely: GwImagesResponse models only {images, providerMetadata}, and gateway_images_parse hardcodes `usage: null` (line 316), though the current AI Gateway image-model v4 protocol returns `usage: {inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens}` and ai.events.Usage can carry input/output tokens today.
findings.evidence: vercel/ai packages/gateway/src/gateway-image-model.ts (fetched from main): `gatewayImageResponseSchema = z.object({ images, warnings: ..., providerMetadata: ..., usage: gatewayImageUsageSchema.optional() })` with `gatewayImageUsageSchema = z.object({ inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens })`. Native class at vercel/ns_internal/images.baml:39-42 has no usage field; parse at :313-317 sets usage: null. sys_llm also dropped it (parse_response/openai/images.rs:49-56, TokenUsage::default) so this is not a regression, but it is a documented capability missing from no deferral list — Usage.total_tokens is in EXECUTION-STATUS's deferred list, but inputTokens/outputTokens fit ai.events.Usage as-is.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `usage: GwImagesUsage?` ({inputTokens, outputTokens} camelCase) to GwImagesResponse and map it into ai.events.Usage in gateway_images_parse.

findings.claim: The gateway client hard-rejects every media input with "Images API only supports text prompts; found image input", but the current gateway image-model v4 protocol supports image editing via `files` and `mask` request fields — the client's own docstring claim "the endpoint has no image-to-image mode" (vercel/images.baml:13-14) is false against current docs.
findings.evidence: vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/image-generation: "You can generate new images from text prompts, edit existing images, and create variations". gateway-image-model.ts doGenerate body: `...(files && { files: files.map(maybeEncodeImageFile) }), ...(mask && { mask: maybeEncodeImageFile(mask) })`. Native _gw_images_prompt_text throws on any media part (vercel/ns_internal/images.baml:107-118). Caveat: this matches the sys_llm ground truth the research report scoped the port to (openai-responses-images.md §2.1: "image-to-image / editing is not supported today"), so it may be accepted scope — but it is not in PLAN §6 or the report's explicit deferral list, and the doc comment overclaims.
findings.suggested_fix: Either lower image prompt parts into `files` (base64 via ai.wire.resolve_media) per the v4 spec, or keep the rejection but fix the docstring to say editing is a not-yet-ported capability of this endpoint.

findings.claim: Gateway response `warnings[]` (typed unsupported/compatibility/deprecated/other warnings in the v4 protocol) are silently discarded — a request whose options the underlying provider ignored looks identical to one fully honored.
findings.evidence: gateway-image-model.ts `gatewayImageWarningSchema` (discriminated union of {type:"unsupported",feature,...}, etc.) is part of gatewayImageResponseSchema; GwImagesResponse (vercel/ns_internal/images.baml:39-42) has no warnings field and nothing logs them.
findings.suggested_fix: Decode warnings and emit them via log.warn in gateway_images_parse.

findings.claim: A missing API key surfaces as an uncatchable panic ("env var not found: OPENAI_API_KEY") rather than an ai.errors.Failure: baml.env.get_or_panic escapes both the client's `catch_all -> ai.errors.normalize` wrapper and the caller's catch_all, so user fallback logic cannot rescue the most common misconfiguration.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe P14: with OPENAI_API_KEY unset and api_key_env pointing at a nonexistent var, the test aborted with `AGGREGATE FAIL ... => env var not found: OPENAI_API_KEY` despite two nested catch_all handlers (openai/images.baml:136-139 normalize wrapper and the probe's own). Same pattern in vercel/images.baml:88. This is the shared cross-client pattern, so it may be a deliberate stdlib-wide decision — flagged because the images clients' error taxonomy is otherwise fully catchable (P7/P10).
findings.suggested_fix: Throw ai.errors.InvalidRequest (or a dedicated AccessError) from resolved_api_key when no credential resolves, instead of get_or_panic.

findings.claim: A gateway `data:` URL without a `;base64,` marker (e.g. `data:image/png,rawpixels`) is silently stored wholesale as the image's base64 payload — user gets an image whose "bytes" are the literal data-URL string.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by probe P11: mock returning {"images":["data:image/png,rawpixels"]} produced `b64=[data:image/png,rawpixels]|mime=[image/png]` with no error. _gw_images_value only special-cases the `;base64,` form and otherwise falls through to from_base64(encoded, fallback_mime).
findings.suggested_fix: When encoded.starts_with("data:") but has no ";base64," marker, throw ai.errors.ParseFailed instead of falling through.

findings.claim: The mixed-shape error message hardcodes the type name "string | image" instead of rendering the declared output type, a small byte-level divergence from sys_llm which rendered `{target}` (lib.rs:856) — visible when the user declared `image | string` or `(string | image)?`.
findings.evidence: Probe P4 output: `Expected one text or image output for string | image, got 2 parts. Use (image | string)[] to preserve mixed outputs.` — identical to sys_llm for the canonical spelling; the other ported messages verified byte-exact (P3 exactly-one via existing test; P3 zero-or-one renders `image | null` via t.to_string(), same union rendering sys_llm's Display used). Cosmetic only; all messages otherwise match sys_llm lib.rs:596-870 verbatim.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `${t.to_string()}` (or the stripped-null form) in the mixed arm's message like the opt arm already does.

findings.claim: The first-class-parameter doc comment is stale against current OpenAI docs: the model catalog now includes gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5 and gpt-image-2 (arbitrary WIDTHxHEIGHT sizes divisible by 16, up to 3840x2160), which the comment's fixed size/quality tables don't mention.
findings.evidence: openai-openapi@master CreateImageRequest: model enum [gpt-image-1.5, dall-e-2, dall-e-3, gpt-image-1, gpt-image-1-mini]; size description: "For gpt-image-2 ... arbitrary resolutions are supported as WIDTHxHEIGHT strings". No wire impact — the client passes strings through and `starts_with("gpt-image")` (ns_internal/images.baml:194) correctly covers all new GPT image models' response_format omission (verified reasoning, not probed live).
findings.suggested_fix: Refresh the comment block; no code change needed.
